discovery: Quantum simulation and quantum information processing with ultracold atoms: theoretical foundations and the realization of programmable many-body quantum matter in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: J. Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Cirac and Zoller showed that controlled atoms can be turned into quantum processors and simulators: their 1995 trapped-ion gate proposal founded the field of experimental quantum computing. Their 1998 work with Jaksch showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models with tunable parameters. Bloch turned this vision into reality with the 2002 observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition. He went on to pioneer single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy and studies of many-body localization, out-of-equilibrium dynamics and topological bands. Together they established a new paradigm: engineering synthetic quantum matter atom by atom to answer questions that classical computers cannot. This program now underpins programmable quantum simulators with ions, lattices and Rydberg tweezer arrays, and it underpins the first error-corrected logical qubits. It connects fundamental many-body physics directly to quantum information science, and its influence is visible in hundreds of laboratories worldwide.
